## e64c021e29ad

**Issue found: arrow position leaks the numeric direction code.** In 900 default
generated grids (300 per band), all 1,488 objects placed the arrow cell on the
same side as the direction encoded by its value: code 1 above, 2 right, 3 below,
and 4 left. The measured correlation is 1,488/1,488; see
`checks/audit/e64c021e29ad_census.json`.

A learner can therefore ignore the code value and sweep toward the side on which
the marker touches the object. That shortcut is not the canonical rule. In the
first canonical training input, code 1 is immediately **left** of the color-6
object but the object sweeps **up**. In the second training input, code 4 is
immediately **right** of the color-5 object but the object sweeps **left**.
Thus the generated distribution systematically teaches a feature that canonical
examples explicitly falsify.

A repair should choose the marker's adjacent side independently of the code and
schedule all code/relative-side combinations, while retaining exactly one
adjacent code per object. No source change was made because this was a
findings-only audit target.
